concerns.location: plan.md:Scope Revision / Phase 1-2; research.md:Modeling Approach step 3-5
concerns.text: The reframed distillation target is a deterministic function of the same text the student sees. The hypothesis 'text implicitly encodes structural information' is then near-tautological: any competent learner can recover features computed from its own input. SC-001 (student MSE vs random-init, p<0.05) is virtually guaranteed and no longer tests anything. The plan must reframe the testable claim (e.g., 'a compact hashed-feature model recovers structure that adds predictive value beyond the baseline text features') and drop/downgrade the distillation-MSE hypothesis as evidence, or justify what non-trivial claim MSE convergence supports.

concerns.location: plan.md:Phase 6 / research.md:Evaluation Plan 'Independence' row; spec FR-008
concerns.text: FR-008's independence ablation is unanswerable in the reframed design: the predicted latent is a deterministic function of the text, so it CANNOT contain information independent of the text-only encoder in the spec's sense. MI/Pearson between latent and text embedding will be confounded by construction. The plan should replace this with an honest reframed criterion (e.g., incremental predictive value of the latent over the baseline embedding, with collinearity reported) and state that FR-008's original independence claim is not executable — currently it is listed as 'addressed in reframed form' without acknowledging the ablation cannot support the independence conclusion.

concerns.location: research.md:Dataset Strategy row; plan.md:Phase 5; data-model.md DocumentPair.label
concerns.text: The downstream construct is 'overlap/CPU-score' with exact column names deferred to download time. If this label is itself a text-overlap metric computed from the same text fields (as the dataset name 'Text-Only Overlap CPU-Score' suggests), the downstream task may reduce to re-deriving a known function of the input — construct validity of 'adds value beyond a text-only baseline' is then questionable and risks leakage. The plan should state what the label is presumed to measure, how it was constructed relative to the text fields, and a pre-registered check (e.g., label-vs-text-similarity correlation) to detect trivial/leaky targets before interpreting the augmented-vs-baseline delta.

The 'capacity-matched baseline' is described inconsistently: an 'identical architecture with a frozen random output head' for the distillation comparison, but the downstream baseline is a text-only embedding + ridge head. Clarify which baseline each paired test uses (SC-001 vs SC-002/SC-003) so the paired t-test pairing unit (seed) and comparison arms are unambiguous.

FR-001 requires visual layout latents from a frozen visual encoder; the plan explicitly marks this 'NOT EXECUTABLE' and substitutes deterministic text-structure features. The spec still mandates the visual encoder, so FR-001 as written has no backing plan element. The plan itself says 'The spec should be amended at the next clarification pass' — the spec is the root cause and must be revised (amend FR-001 or add a reframed FR) before the plan can claim coverage.

FR-004 mandates concatenating text embeddings with 'predicted visual latents'; the plan substitutes predicted structural latents. Same spec-root mismatch as FR-001 — the spec text still requires the visual latent and is not covered by any plan element as written.

FR-005 and US-3 specify evaluation on 'held-out scientific reasoning tasks (e.g., table QA)'. The plan's Phase 5 evaluates prediction of the dataset's overlap/CPU-score label instead. This is a substantive redefinition of the downstream task with no corresponding spec amendment; the spec's ReasoningTask entity and table-QA scenario are unbacked.

US-1 scenario 2 requires the latent to differ from a text-only baseline by cosine similarity ≥ 0.1 or KL ≥ 0.05. No plan element measures this; with the visual encoder dropped, this acceptance scenario is silently uncovered and needs explicit removal/replacement in the spec.

The spec's dataset assumption names 'llmXive-layout-distillation', 'layout-parser' fallback, and 'pubmed-layout' — all shown unobtainable. The spec still asserts these sources exist; it must be amended to the single verified parquet URL so FR-007/SC-006's 'primary + fallback sources' wording matches the plan's single-source design.

Key Entities define VisualLatent as derived from the frozen visual encoder and DistilledModel as a 50M-parameter Transformer; the plan's StructuralLatent entity and hashed-feature MLP student diverge. Once FR-001/FR-004 are amended, update these entity definitions for consistency.

The reframed target is 'deterministic structural feature vectors' (line counts, mean line length, heading/list markers, whitespace ratios) computed from the text of the MixSub-LLaMA-3.2 Text-Only Overlap CPU-Score parquet. That dataset is a text-overlap/score corpus; there is no cited evidence its text fields preserve line-level structure (newlines, headings, list markers). If the text is stored as flattened single-line strings, the structural extractor will produce near-constant/degenerate targets and the distillation study is vacuous. Add an explicit data-sufficiency check at preprocess time (e.g. variance/non-degeneracy assertion on the structural feature matrix, with graceful failure per FR-007) and name the fallback if the check fails, so the plan does not silently run on degenerate targets.

The plan drops the visual-encoder component of FR-001/FR-004 and replaces visual latents with text-derived structural features, but the constitution's Principle VII makes 'visual layout latents (generated by a frozen visual encoder)' the project's primary scientific contribution, and the spec (FR-001, US-1) still mandates it. The plan itself admits 'The spec should be amended at the next clarification pass' — but no amendment exists yet, so plan, spec, and constitution currently disagree on the core mechanism. Downstream task verification against the unamended spec FR-001 will fail. Either amend the spec/constitution (scope-limitation clause for Principle VII) before plan acceptance, or route this through the clarification pass now.

Data-model defines StructuralLatent as a separate entity keyed by doc_id, but the schema and data flow embed the latent as an optional `structural_latent` column inside DocumentPair (document_pairs_with_latent.parquet). These are two different representations; pick one (or state the parquet column is the serialized form of the StructuralLatent entity) so contract tests and the data model agree.

Plan/research use Bonferroni α = 0.025 for the two primary hypotheses, while spec SC-003 defines success as p < 0.05. The plan should explicitly note the Bonferroni-corrected threshold is stricter than and consistent with SC-003's 0.05 standard, or the discrepancy will look like a contract mismatch at task-verification time.

The reframed distillation hypothesis is near-tautological. The target is a deterministic function of the input text ('structural feature vectors computed from the text itself via a fixed pipeline'), and the student predicts it from that same text. A model with sufficient capacity learning a fixed deterministic function of its own input will essentially always beat a random-init baseline on val MSE — the '5% lower MSE, p<0.05' success criterion (SC-001) can only be confirmed, never falsified. This is a circular validation: the target is determined by the predictor's input. The plan needs a genuinely held-out or independent target, or must reframe SC-001 as a sanity check rather than a hypothesis test.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 6 / FR-008 ablation ('independence check (MI / Pearson r between latent and text embedding)')
concerns.text: FR-008 requires demonstrating the predicted latents 'contain information independent of the text-only encoder.' In the reframed design the latent is BY CONSTRUCTION a function of the text (student(text) → structural features of text), so it cannot contain information independent of the text representation. The planned MI/Pearson check can only ever show dependence; the ablation is definitionally unsatisfiable. The plan acknowledges collinearity descriptively but still maps FR-008 as 'addressed in reframed form' — it is not addressable in this design and should be marked NOT EXECUTABLE alongside FR-001/FR-004, not reported as a pass/fail ablation.

concerns.location: research.md: Dataset Strategy / downstream task ('predicting the dataset's overlap/CPU-score signal')
concerns.text: The downstream label comes from a 'Text-Only Overlap CPU-Score' dataset — the label may itself be a deterministic or near-deterministic function of text overlap (e.g., n-gram/substring overlap between text fields). If so, the downstream task is solvable from surface text features and any 'gain' from structural latents is uninterpretable; if the label is computed from the same text fields used as input, the evaluation risks leakage. The plan should state the label's semantics (what the overlap/CPU-score measures and from which columns) and justify that it is not a trivial function of the input text before using it as the outcome variable.

concerns.location: plan.md: Scope Revision ('does plain text implicitly encode structural information...')
concerns.text: Construct drift: the reframed question ('can a model distill text-computable features from text?') is a different, much weaker claim than the spec's/constitution's Principle VII claim (visual layout latents transfer). The plan is honest about the scope limitation, but the surviving study as designed does not test 'text implicitly encodes structure' in any meaningful sense — the structure is explicitly computable from text by a documented extractor. The research question should be restated to match what is actually testable (e.g., 'do cheap structural summary features add predictive value over dense text features for the overlap label?'), so the final report's claims match the analysis.

responses.response: Reframed the testable claim: the primary hypothesis is now the downstream incremental-predictive-value test (structural summary features add predictive value beyond dense text features for the overlap label). The distillation MSE convergence (SC-001) is explicitly downgraded to a sanity/feasibility check, not hypothesis evidence, with the circularity stated.

responses.response: FR-008's independence claim is now marked NOT EXECUTABLE (the latent is by construction a function of the text). Replaced with an honest reframed criterion: incremental predictive value of the latent over the baseline embedding, with collinearity (MI/Pearson) reported descriptively as confounded-by-construction.

responses.response: Added a pre-registered label-semantics and leakage check: before interpreting the downstream delta, the pipeline records the label's construction (columns, semantics from provenance.json), computes a label-vs-surface-text-similarity correlation, and flags the downstream result as uninterpretable if the label is a trivial function of input text. If flagged, the study reports the leakage finding instead of claiming an augmented-vs-baseline gain.

The frozen-head model is used only for the SC-001 sanity check, never for downstream.
